paras: The attempted lynching of Bud Wilson took place on August 22, 1900, when a mob of white men chased a St. Joseph, Missouri, police officer and his Black prisoner for about a mile through the Chicago Great Western Railroad yards. According to the only report found, the officer's protection kept Wilson from being lynched, and he was afterward held at the police station.

Wilson, described as "a negro prisoner, aged 18 years," was accused of stabbing M. F. Lyon, a brakeman, in the abdomen. The dispatch said Wilson had been "stealing a ride" on the railroad, and it gave no other account of how the stabbing happened.

Police Officer Kieffer had Wilson in custody when "a mob of infuriated white men" pursued them through the yards. The chase covered about a mile, and the report credited the officer's "efforts to protect his prisoner" with saving Wilson from the mob. No injury to Wilson or the officer was reported, and no member of the mob was named.

Wilson was placed in a cell at the police station to await the outcome of Lyon's injuries. No report of Lyon's condition, of a charge or trial against Wilson, or of arrests among the mob appears in the coverage.

The episode survives in a single "Republic Special" dispatch printed on page 5 of the St. Louis Republic on August 23, 1900, among other short regional items. Its headline, "MOB AFTER A NEGRO," and subhead, "St. Joseph Policeman Protected His Prisoner During a Mile Run," made the officer's conduct the point of the story. The dispatch stated the stabbing as fact ("stabbed by him") rather than as a charge, and it offered no comment on the mob. No account of the episode was found in the Black press or in other white papers in the weeks that followed.

reader.title: Attempted lynching of Bud Wilson
bases: A1 reports a mob of white men pursuing a Black prisoner and says he would have been lynched but for the officer, an attempted lynching with no one killed.

A1 reports that the mob chased Wilson but the officer protected him and he was held in a police cell, so no one was killed; the case is an attempted lynching, not a lynching under the standard definition.
The only report found is one special dispatch in the St. Louis Republic (A1); no local, follow-up or Black-press account was found.

accounts.label: Republic special dispatch
accounts.gist: A white mob chased Officer Kieffer and his prisoner Wilson a mile through the Chicago Great Western yards; the officer's efforts kept Wilson from being lynched, and Wilson was jailed pending the outcome of the brakeman's wound.

quotes: A mob of infuriated white men chased Police Officer Kieffer and Bud Wilson, a negro prisoner, aged 18 years, for a distance of a mile through the Chicago Great Western Railroad yards.
But for the officer's efforts to protect his prisoner, Wilson would have been lynched.
The negro is in a cell at the police station awaiting the outcome of injuries inflicted upon M. F. Lyon, a brakeman, who was stabbed by him in the abdomen.
